subject: Dedicated GPU pool rightsizing for high-concurrency conversational product
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@cobaltai.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procure@cobaltai.com, devops@cobaltai.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity needs + pricing request for conversational product

Hi Logan / Ben,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. We need a concise sizing + committed pricing proposal from Redwood for our conversational assistant. High-level workload below — I attached the CSV with per-endpoint breakdown. Can you confirm: recommended GPU pool size, expected throughput (p95 latency target), and reserved-commit pricing (monthly) including discount tiers and rollover/burst mechanics?

Quick profile:
- Peak concurrent active sessions (in-flight requests): 420–500 (30 min morning spike)
- Average sustained RPS: 650 reqs/sec globally (US primary)
- Average request: 1.2k user tokens in, 500 tokens out (~1700 total context)
- LLM model: mix of a 13B instruction-tuned open model and a smaller 7B reranker; primary served on the larger model
- P95 latency target: <= 600 ms (generation end-to-end)
- SLA needs: 99.9% uptime; audit logs and isolation for our sensitive endpoints
- Start timeline: want dedicated pool live in Q1 2027; open to 12-month commit but want pilot/POC first

Also include: onboarding timeline, monitoring hooks (token-level cost breakdown), and suggested fallback/quantization options to reduce commit size.

Procurement is looped (procure@cobaltai.com) — they want the monthly committed spend to review with finance.

Appreciate a concise one-pager we can take to the CFO.

Best,
Anna Park
Head of ML Products
Cobalt AI

Attachment: cobalt_workload_profile.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@cobaltai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs + pricing request for conversational product

Anna — thanks, got the CSV and the high level is clear. Quick clarifying questions before we size:
1) Is the 650 RPS number steady-state or an average across all endpoints? If it’s weighted, can you call out what percent of traffic goes to the 13B vs the 7B reranker?
2) Tokenization and sampling settings: avg decoding tokens per response you gave as ~500 — are you using temperature 0.7 top_p 0.9? This affects tail latency.
3) Do you expect many streaming responses, or are most responses returned in a single final payload?

Initial assumptions we’ll use for the first pass:
- 70% of requests hit the 13B model; 30% are light reranks on the 7B
- Average total context ~1.7k tokens, with sampling that produces ~500 decoding tokens, non-streamed 90% of the time
- Target p95 <= 600ms for generation step only (we’ll include network buffer in SLO)

I’ll coordinate with Ben and Marissa to produce a 1-page rightsizing + pricing sheet. Can we jump on a 30-min call tomorrow 9–11 PT to align on prioritization and pilot scope?

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 09:12 Anna Park <anna@cobaltai.com> wrote:
> (original message and attachment)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@cobaltai.com>, procure@cobaltai.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity needs + pricing request for conversational product

Anna / procurement team — following our assumptions above, here is a concrete starting proposal for committed Dedicated capacity and pricing. This is a commercial-first, conservative estimate to meet your P95 target for a 13B-style open model.

Sizing recommendation (initial commit):
- Recommended starting pool: 6 x H100-class GPUs (80GB-equivalent) dedicated to Cobalt AI
  - Rationale: with our serving runtime and batching, 6 GPUs handle ~650 sustained RPS with peak bursts to ~1.1k RPS while holding ~550–600 ms p95 for ~1.7k-token contexts (13B). We model 70/30 split (13B/7B); the 7B reranker runs on a shared quantized fleet with minimal impact.
  - If you want a smaller commitment with the same SLO, we can use 4 GPUs + autoscaling to hosted capacity for peaks (higher overage unit cost).

Commercials (monthly committed pricing):
- List rate (reference): $28,000 per GPU / month (H100-equivalent)
- 12-month reserved commit (standard): 18% discount -> $22,960 / GPU / month
  - 6 GPUs @ 12 months = $137,760 / month (committed)
- 24-month reserved commit: 22% discount -> $21,840 / GPU / month
  - 6 GPUs @ 24 months = $131,040 / month
- Pilot option (recommended): 3-month pilot at 4 GPUs, pro-rated monthly at 15% below list (pilot price = $23,800 / GPU / month) -> 4 GPUs = $95,200 / month for pilot period

Burst/overage and rollover mechanics:
- Bursts above committed pool are covered by: (1) burst capacity from Redwood Hosted at an overage rate (negotiable; baseline $0.09 / 1k tokens generated), or (2) automatic fallbacks to a quantized 13B variant (avg quality delta ~2–4% depending on prompts) to reduce token compute and keep latency in SLO.
- Unused committed GPU hours are converted to account credits at 60% of the pro-rated committed price and can be applied to burst usage or saved toward future months (one-month lookback).

SLA and ops:
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool. We include support windows, on-call routing, and a runbook for failover to hosted variants.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and model-quality monitoring (we’ll ingest a small eval set you provide).

Next steps / timeline:
1) Sign pilot SOW (3 months, 4 GPUs) — we’ll validate throughput and p95 on your traffic patterns (2–3 weeks testing cadence).
2) If pilot meets SLOs, convert to 12-month commit for 6 GPUs with a 30-day notice to scale.
3) Provide DocuSign + SOW for legal review (I attached a term sheet).

I’ve attached a short pricing term sheet and an SOW draft. Happy to jump on a call to explain the math.

— Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_term_sheet.xlsx, redwood_sow_v1.pdf
From: Anna Park <anna@cobaltai.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: procure@cobaltai.com, devops@cobaltai.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs + pricing request for conversational product

Thanks Ben — that’s helpful and detailed. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

Procurement notes: the monthly $137k number for 6 GPUs is higher than expected; CFO is looking for a path to cap committed spend in Q1 until we prove unit economics. They prefer a 12-month commit but want to cap initial monthly liability to ~$80k.

Engineering notes: we need clearer latency modeling for streaming responses and the impact of prompt engineering (dynamic truncation). Can the pilot demonstrate the streaming p95 as well? Also confirm how quick scale-to-peak is handled (minutes vs hours).

Proposed counter:
- Start with a 3-month pilot at 4 GPUs (as you suggested) but at an effective monthly pilot spend cap of $80k (we’ll pay pro-rated and the remainder should be credits applied to future committed months).
- Pilot must include streaming p95 tests and staged traffic shaping to replicate morning spikes.

If Redwood can accept that commercial structure, procurement will share a PO and we can move forward quickly.

Anna
Anna Park
Head of ML Products, Cobalt AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@cobaltai.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procure@cobaltai.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs + pricing request for conversational product

Anna — we can accommodate that counter with a pilot structure that protects Cobalt’s initial spend while giving us the signal we need to rightsized final commit. Proposed pilot commercial and technical scope below.

Pilot commercial terms (3 months):
- Pool: 4 x H100-class GPUs dedicated
- Monthly pilot invoice: $80,000 / month (Cobalt cap). Redwood will record the difference between our standard pilot charge ($95,200 / month) and the $80k you pay as a one-time account credit that can be applied to the first committed month when you convert to a 12-month deal.
- Deliverables: test report, SLO verification (streaming + final generation p95), and an ops runbook.

Technical + ops commitments:
- Stage 1 (week 1–2): deploy pool, mirror sampled production traffic (non-PII), baseline measurements.
- Stage 2 (week 3–6): stress tests for morning spike patterns (simulate 420–500 concurrent sessions), streaming scenarios, and model fallback verification.
- Stage 3 (week 7–12): run-for-purpose with live traffic routing for validation and handover to your ops.
- Scale-to-peak: the pool will auto-burst to Redwood Hosted capacity for short (minutes-level) spikes via async provisioning; for sustained >30-min peaks we recommend conversion to larger commit or a scheduled scale window.

Next steps:
1) I’ll update the SOW to reflect the pilot cap and the credit mechanics and circulate for signature (DocuSign link will be included).
2) Schedule kickoff: propose Dec 15 for initial deployment and testing — does that align with your timeline?

If that works, procurement can route the PO to procure@cobaltai.com and we’ll get legal looped in.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Platform for production LLM inference

Attachment: redwood_sow_v1.pdf (SOW draft)
